A.explanation: Constant speed means kinetic energy is constant, but work is still done against the $2100\text{ N}$ resistive force and appears as thermal energy.

B.explanation: This is $900 \times 25 = 2.3 \times 10^4\text{ W}$, the rate of gain of gravitational potential energy against the weight component, not the thermal dissipation.

C.explanation: Thermal power equals resistive force times speed: $2100 \times 25 = 52500\text{ W} \approx 5.3 \times 10^4\text{ W}$.

D.explanation: This is $3000 \times 25 = 7.5 \times 10^4\text{ W}$, the total power supplied by the engine, which splits into thermal dissipation plus gravitational potential energy.

hints: Notice the $2100\text{ N}$ total force due to air resistance and friction and the constant $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ speed up the slope.
Recall that rate of working against a force at constant speed is $P = Fv$, so only the dissipative force counts for thermal power.
Multiply $2100\text{ N}$ by $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and check why the $3000\text{ N}$ drive force and $900\text{ N}$ weight component are not used for this part.
walkthrough: Identify the dissipative force: air resistance plus friction is $F = 2100\text{ N}$ opposing the motion at speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the power rule: rate of energy transfer by a constant force moving with the object is $P = Fv$.
Apply it to the resistive force only: $P_{thermal} = 2100 \times 25$.
Calculate with units: $P_{thermal} = 52500\text{ W} \approx 5.3 \times 10^4\text{ W}$, which is a power in $\text{W}$ as required.

Note the energy balance: engine power $3000 \times 25 = 7.5 \times 10^4\text{ W}$ equals thermal $5.25 \times 10^4\text{ W}$ plus potential $900 \times 25 = 2.25 \times 10^4\text{ W}$. This is option C
